text.p: Business came to a virtual standstill on Tuesday across southeast Bangladesh where the opposition Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) called a daylong strike, local officials and witnesses said.

BNP chief Begum Khaleda Zia called for the dawn-to-dusk stoppage to protest against what she said was "government-led terrorism and the ruling (Awami League) party's subservient policies towards India."
Khaleda has accused Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina of being pro-Indian, jeopardising Bangladesh's national security.

Transport stopped in Chittagong port city and 10 neighbouring districts, witnesses said, although one flight from Dhaka landed in Chittagong early in the day. Schools, offices and businesses were all closed.
Work at the main port was partially affected, said Captain Zahiruddin Mahmud, chairman of the Chittagong Port Authority.
Sporadic blasts of home-made bombs and crackers forced residents to stay at home, witnesses said.
"This is a near-total strike," said one Chittagong journalist who went round the city.
Khaleda said she called the strike only in the greater Chittagong division because that was the area most affected by "government-led terrorism". She did not elaborate.
The BNP says the government has been persecuting political opponents, jailing thousands.
One senior BNP official said last week ruling party thugs had killed nearly 200 party workers and supporters since it came to power last June, a charge the government denies.
Khaleda said on Saturday that May 6 would "serve as a warning to this autocratic government and will be followed up, if necessary, with tougher actions."
The strike did not affect other parts of the country.
